explanation: Retrospective detector of function words in concrete, practical text: it reads 1.5-3.5 on a preposition, article, numeral, 'and' or list comma that continues a description of placing, mixing, measuring, packaging, selling or locating physical things ('mix with a', 'on a tray', 'available in three', '1lb per', 'for 20', 'in the oven', the commas in 'sugar, butter, eggs'), on perfect/possessive 'has/have' after a noun subject, on ';' or '")' closing a code header ('using System;'), and on nearly every French or Italian preposition or article (de, la, dans, au, avec, son, in, di) whatever follows. It stays below ~0.9 on all content words (nouns, most verbs, adjectives ~0), on sentence-final periods (~0.75), and on function words and commas in social, narrative or abstract English where the slots hold people, pronouns, feelings or ideas ('talk with a friend', 'give the letter to the boy', 'Sarah, Peter, Emma', 'interested in politics', 'theory of justice'), with occasional 1.0-1.5 blips there; note the first token of any text reads 0.6-1.1 ('The' 0.94, 'Please' 1.02), so a text starting that way is weakly active on its first token only.
